stories.summary: The Trump administration has proposed new tariffs on 14 trading partners after an eight-month Section 301 probe into excess industrial capacity; Singapore would face up to 20% on all goods, with exemptions, but the USTR says it would consider 10% if Singapore reaches a reciprocal trade agreement or resolves the issues raised. Public hearings come first, with duties likely from January.
stories.title: US proposes tariffs of up to 20% on Singapore goods — but the rate could fall to 10% with a trade deal
stories.why: Singapore is directly in the firing line of the rebuilt US tariff wall, and the 10% offer gives the government a negotiating lever.

stories.summary: StarHub will issue about 651.7 million new shares to M1 shareholders, who will own 27.4% of the enlarged group; Keppel will hold an effective 23% stake. The merged business would have pro forma revenue of about S$2.6 billion and target S$110 million in annual cost synergies by 2030. Completion is expected in the first half of 2027, subject to IMDA and shareholder approvals.
stories.title: StarHub and M1 agree all-share merger to create a 4.1 million-customer telecoms group
stories.why: It cuts Singapore's mobile network operators from four to three and reshapes the market.

stories.summary: MTI raised the 2026 growth forecast to around 6% after third-quarter GDP was revised up to 6.1% year on year, and expects 2.5% to 4.5% growth in 2027. AI-related electronics, manufacturing and wholesale trade are driving growth, while retail, F&B and tourism-linked sectors remain soft.
stories.title: Singapore raises 2026 GDP growth forecast to around 6% as AI boom powers the economy
stories.why: The AI investment cycle is now the main engine of Singapore's growth — and the reason behind the bumper civil service bonus.

stories.summary: All civil servants will receive a 1.55-month year-end bonus, with junior-grade officers getting an extra one-time payment of S$300 or S$600; with the mid-year bonus, total variable pay for 2026 comes to two months, plus the one-month 13th-month payment.
stories.title: Civil servants to get 1.55-month year-end bonus, the biggest since at least 2006
stories.why: The payout reflects the upgraded ~6% growth forecast and sets a benchmark for private-sector year-end bonuses.

stories.summary: AP Oil group CEO Ho Chee Hon, 49, was sentenced to six months' jail after driving against traffic on Peirce Road for about 12 seconds and crashing into a drain; his breath-alcohol reading was 97 micrograms, nearly three times the legal limit. He was fined S$25,000 and banned from driving for nine years; he starts jail on 1 December and the company has named an acting CEO.
stories.title: AP Oil CEO jailed six months for drink-driving against traffic and crashing into a drain
stories.why: A listed-company chief jailed for a repeat drink-driving offence — a corporate governance story as much as a court one.

stories.summary: The FCC authorised SpaceX's Starmind constellation of up to 1 million satellites to operate as data centres in space, the first US authorisation of its kind; SpaceX must launch its first satellite by November 2033 and the full constellation by 2040. The approval came despite objections from Amazon, Viasat and astronomers, and the FCC deferred a decision on debris disposal for higher orbits.
stories.title: FCC approves SpaceX plan to launch 1 million satellites for orbital AI data centres
stories.why: It is the first regulatory green light for moving AI compute into orbit — a new front in the AI infrastructure race.

stories.summary: OpenAI is piloting Private Inference with a small group of business customers, letting them run queries on its most powerful models without OpenAI being able to access the data, using isolated hardware with verifiable controls. It is part of OpenAI Private Intelligence and is in alpha, with no date for a wider rollout.
stories.title: OpenAI starts testing Private Inference so business prompts stay sealed while models run
stories.why: Confidential computing could unlock AI for sensitive enterprise and government work — including defence and intelligence customers.

stories.summary: The Nasdaq fell more than 4% early in Wednesday's session before dip buyers stepped in, ending down 0.62% at 23,585.80; the S&P 500 lost 0.25% and the Dow rose 0.33%. The Nasdaq is down 7.3% for November as doubts grow over AI spending and returns.
stories.title: Nvidia drops 4% as AI sell-off resumes, but Wall Street ends well off the day's lows
stories.why: The AI trade — the market's central pillar — is faltering, and Nvidia's slide is the clearest signal.

stories.summary: Asian stocks looked poised for modest gains after a late Wall Street recovery pulled the Nasdaq 100 back from a 20% drop below its peak; the S&P 500 closed 0.3% lower and the Dow gained 0.3%. Ten-year Treasury yields fell for an eighth straight day, gold bounced back, and Brent rose over 3% to under US$95 a barrel.
stories.title: Asian stocks set for gains after late US rebound pulls Nasdaq 100 back from bear market
stories.why: Dip-buying is still cushioning the AI sell-off, but volatility gauges show markets remain stressed.

stories.summary: Investors rushed to safe havens as the new US tariff proposals hit markets already reeling from the AI rout; the Nasdaq fell 2% on Wednesday and is down almost 20% from its early-October record, the VIX has soared more than 60% in November, and chip stocks have fallen 50% from June's record. US markets are closed on Thursday for Thanksgiving.
stories.title: Volatility-weary investors hammered as tariff mayhem adds to tech pain
stories.why: Tariffs and the AI correction are compounding into one of the sharpest volatility spikes since COVID.

stories.summary: BNP Paribas moved up the Financial Stability Board's 2026 list of global systemically important banks, raising its required capital buffer to 2% from 1.5% from January 2028; MUFG was the only other mover, down to 1%. JPMorgan remains the most systemically important bank at 2.5%, and the list stays at 29 banks.
stories.title: BNP Paribas moves up global systemic bank list; capital buffer rises to 2%
stories.why: Higher buffers for Europe's biggest banks tighten the capital backdrop for global lending.

stories.summary: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz told the Bundestag that Russia is escalating in the Baltic, Poland, the Black Sea, space and inside Germany itself, as he defended plans to double defence spending to over €200 billion by 2030 and maintain military aid to Ukraine. A poll showed a narrow majority of Germans now oppose the aid.
stories.title: 'Russia wants more than Ukraine,' Merz says as he defends aid for Kyiv
stories.why: Europe's biggest military backer of Ukraine is doubling down even as public support frays.

stories.summary: Russian forces launched a late-night ballistic missile attack on Kyiv, striking a shopping mall and two other buildings in the Desnianskyi district; four people were injured, two seriously. The attack came a day after President Zelenskyy said 48 funded Patriot interceptors were still awaiting the US defence secretary's signature.
stories.title: Russia hits Kyiv shopping mall with ballistic missiles, injuring four
stories.why: Civilian targets are being hit while Kyiv waits on air-defence ammunition.

stories.summary: German media reported that Western intelligence assesses Russia could launch its "Sputnik-S" satellite — built to carry a nuclear weapon — within 60 days, possibly in December; Le Monde reports the risk is considered serious in Paris. A nuclear detonation in orbit could disable about a third of low-Earth-orbit satellites and would violate the 1967 Outer Space Treaty.
stories.title: Risk of Russia launching a nuclear weapon into space within two months deemed serious
stories.why: A space-based nuclear weapon would threaten the satellites underpinning communications, navigation and finance.

stories.summary: Iran's UN envoy told the Security Council that US forces used Palantir's Maven, Anthropic's Claude and Grok to analyse intelligence and select targets during the February 2026 war, claiming 2,000 munitions were used on 2,000 targets in 96 hours. He cited the Minab school strike and called for UN governance of military AI. The claims are Iran's and have not been independently verified.
stories.title: Iran tells UN the US used AI to pick targets in the February war
stories.why: It is the first time a state has used the Security Council to demand accountability for AI-enabled targeting.

stories.summary: The Army carried out a controlled detonation of 9,500 pounds of degraded, dangerously unstable lead azide at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant after days of legal challenges; the EPA said all real-time air monitors showed zero airborne lead, and an all-clear was issued about nine hours later. Soil, surface and water sampling continues, and about 350 farms lie in the plume area.
stories.title: US Army detonates 9,500 pounds of unstable lead azide in Iowa; air monitors show zero lead
stories.why: The operation eliminated the risk of an uncontrolled blast from the military's last stockpile of the explosive — but questions remain over how it was allowed to deteriorate.

stories.summary: A joint OCCRP/Delfi investigation found Russia's Doppelgänger network produced 1,800 articles from more than 500 interviews with European and Western politicians, turning genuine statements into pro-Moscow propaganda through outlets like Recent Reliable News. The network kept obtaining interviews into autumn 2026, and the EU has sanctioned its operator, the Social Design Agency.
stories.title: How Russia's Doppelgänger network used 500 interviews to influence Europe
stories.why: It shows how influence operations now launder real voices instead of fabricating news — making them far harder to debunk.

stories.summary: A 30-year-old man pleaded guilty to transmitting a false message after he used Gemini to add a crocodile to a photo of Pandan Reservoir; the image reached PUB officers, prompting search operations and the suspension of water activities. Prosecutors are seeking six to seven weeks' jail, and sentencing is on 1 December.
stories.title: Man pleads guilty after fake AI crocodile photo triggers searches at Pandan Reservoir
stories.why: A single AI-generated image mobilised government agencies — a small, concrete example of synthetic media's real-world cost.

tldr: US proposes tariffs of up to 20% on Singapore goods — but the rate could fall to 10% if a trade deal is reached.
FCC clears SpaceX to put 1 million AI data-centre satellites into orbit.
Asian stocks set to gain after Wall Street's late rebound pulls the Nasdaq 100 back from bear-market territory.
Merz warns "Russia wants more than Ukraine" as he defends aid for Kyiv and a doubling of German defence spending.
Russia's Doppelgänger network turned 500 interviews with Western politicians into 1,800 pro-Moscow articles.
